item.title: Argentina Extends $6 Billion in Repo Maturities Beyond Election
item.description: Argentina’s central bank extended maturities worth $6 billion on its repurchase agreements — or repos — to ease the government debt burden going into the 2027 presidential election.

item.title: Canadian Stocks Enjoy Broad Gains After New Pipeline Proposal
item.description: Canada’s stocks benchmark climbed Friday morning after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled a new pipeline project to the country’s West Coast.

item.title: OPEC Output Surged in June as Hormuz Flows Jumped, Survey Shows
item.description: OPEC’s crude oil production surged last month as Persian Gulf members restored exports through the Strait of Hormuz amid a peace accord between the US and Iran, according to a Bloomberg survey.

item.title: Fed and ECB Seen Diverging in French Snapshot of War Aftermath
item.description: The Federal Reserve will still need to hike interest rates this year despite Thursday’s numbers pointing to labor-market weakness, according to two French chief economists.

item.title: GFL Environmental Weighs Take-Private Amid Interest From Buyout Firms
item.description: GFL Environmental Inc. is considering a potential take-private transaction after drawing interest from buyout firms, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Xi Replaces Anti-Corruption Leader in Purge of China’s Army
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping has appointed a new head of anti-corruption efforts in the armed forces as he continues the country’s biggest military purge in half a century.

item.title: African Economies Bounce Back as Energy Prices Tumble, PMIs Show
item.description: African economies from South Africa to Kenya bounced back in June and may get a further boost in coming months as the economic toll of the Iran conflict dissipates.

item.title: Carlyle Hires Banks for $400 Million India IPO of RCM Business
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. has hired JM Financial Ltd. and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. to advise on a potential initial public offering of its India-based healthcare revenue cycle management business, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: iCON Infrastructure to Buy Northern Fiber in Rescue Deal
item.description: Lenders of Northern Fiber Holding GmbH, a struggling German fiber-network operator formerly owned by UBS Asset Management, are finalizing the sale of the company to iCON Infrastructure to avoid a looming insolvency.

item.title: Russia Hikes June Subsidies to Refiners as Fuel Shortages Bite
item.description: Russia’s subsidy payouts to oil refiners that supply domestic markets jumped more than six-fold in June from a year earlier, as Moscow sought to avoid shortages by keeping more fuel at home.

item.title: Americans Drive Into July 4 Holiday With Gas Prices Still Stinging
item.description: Independence Day period set to be third-most expensive for US drivers on record.

item.title: EU Agrees to Cut ESG Reporting Requirements for Asset Managers
item.description: Money managers in Europe won’t have to report ESG data on all the assets they hold, under revised disclosure requirements.

item.title: What Natural Gas’s Ascendancy Says About the US
item.description: Fracking, booming power demand and enthusiastic political support have underpinned the fuel’s rise, but for how long?

item.title: Adani Group Secures $15 Billion Capital This Week as US Legal Clouds Clear
item.description: In one week, billionaire Gautam Adani has announced nearly $15 billion in investment commitments across its ports, mining and flagship businesses.

item.title: CVC Plans €1.2 Billion of High-Yield Bonds to Fund Irca Buyout
item.description: CVC Capital Partners Plc is set to finance its buyout of Italian food-ingredients maker Irca SpA with €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) of high-yield bonds, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Big Tech Sends Workers Into the Field to Help Customers Use AI
item.description: Microsoft, Amazon follow AI companies by creating units of “forward-deployed” engineers

item.title: How the AI Boom Is Carving a K-Shape Into Asian Economies
item.description: Ties to the data-center build-out are benefiting the region.

item.title: China’s State Iron Ore Buyer Extends Restrictions on Fortescue
item.description: China’s state-backed iron ore buyer has expanded its curbs on Fortescue Ltd.’s iron ore to include new purchases of its Super Special Fines product and not just portside inventories, escalating its dispute with the Australian miner.

item.title: Indonesia’s Danantara Wealth Fund Sees Senior Management Shakeup
item.description: Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara is reshuffling its management team with a series of new hires, according to people familiar with the matter, as it expands its role under President Prabowo Subianto’s government.

item.title: Investors Warm to Burnham But Say Long-End Gilts Are ‘Unloved’
item.description: UK bond investors are gaining confidence in Andy Burnham’s promises of discipline when it comes to borrowing and spending, but not enough to bet on Britain’s long-dated debt.

item.title: Gulf Carriers Eye Boeing, Airbus Jets as Air India Weighs Delays
item.description: Airlines in the Persian Gulf are looking to snap up earlier delivery slots for Boeing Co. and Airbus SE aircraft that may be freed up as Air India Ltd. discusses potentially deferring some orders, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Investors Track Tokens for Clues on AI Trade’s Next Move
item.description: Investors are tracking AI token prices as they try to figure out where the volatile trade goes next.

item.title: ECB Is in ‘Good Position’ After June Rate Hike, Moulin Says
item.description: The European Central Bank is in a comfortable situation after last month’s interest-rate increase as the falling oil price eases price pressures in the euro zone, Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said.

item.title: At 17, She Sued Meta and Google, and Won. Now She’s Ready to Tell Her Story
item.description: Kaley Glenn-Mills’ lawsuit reshaped the fight to protect children from social media. She says she still can’t stop scrolling.

item.title: Video Games in Europe Face New Restrictions on Age, ‘Loot Boxes’
item.description: The video-game industry is bracing for a wave of European regulations that could limit kids’ access to some video games, potentially crimping sales across the globe.

item.title: Russia’s Oil-Port City on Black Sea Is Fast Running Out of Fuel
item.description: Novorossiysk, home to Russia’s largest oil port on the Black Sea, is running out of road fuel, the latest fallout from a supply crunch spreading across the country as Ukraine continues attacks on key refineries.

item.title: Danish Krone’s Slide Raises Question: What’s Central Bank Up To?
item.description: The Danish krone is trading at all-time lows against the euro, fueling speculation that the central bank has shifted its strategy for defending the peg.

item.title: US Stocks Post Largest Outflows in Over Three Months, BofA Says
item.description: Investors are turning away from US stocks at the fastest pace since March, according to Bank of America Corp.

item.title: HSBC, Standard Chartered Weigh SRTs as Asia-Linked Deals Ramp Up
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc is laying the groundwork for a significant risk transfer linked to a portfolio of Asia-Pacific loans as it ramps up use of the hedging instrument.

item.title: UK Firms Expect to Raise Prices 4% Even as Inflation Falls
item.description: UK companies became more optimistic about inflation in June, even as they plan to raise their own prices by 4% in the coming year — double the Bank of England’s CPI target.
